titel: A New Translation of a Master Filmmaker: Dr. Anne McKnight on Long Take

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Translating Akira Kurosawa's candid conversations, film lists, and memoirs
kurzfassung: Dr. Anne McKnight discusses her new English translation of 'Long Take', a book featuring interviews, roundtables, and a curated list of favorite films by Akira Kurosawa. The conversation explores Kurosawa's working methods, his deep appreciation for literature and silent cinema, and the challenges of capturing his distinct voice. Additionally, McKnight shares insights from the book's concluding section written by Kurosawa's daughter, Kazuko.
stichpunkte: Dr. Anne McKnight translates 'Long Take', offering the first English version of post-mortem interviews, essays, and roundtables concerning Akira Kurosawa.
The book includes a chronology and a list of Kurosawa's 100 favorite films, curated through the memory of his daughter Kazuko.
Kurosawa was known as an unwilling interview subject who rarely discussed his films in granular detail.
To accurately translate his voice, McKnight watched nearly every film and read the literature referenced in the text.
The translation preserves Japanese honorifics like san and kun to reflect the distinct professional and personal relationships among directors.
Kurosawa approached every movie first as a silent film, demonstrating a deep stylistic debt to early cinematic movement and composition.
Beyond Hollywood westerns, Kurosawa drew heavily on Russian problem literature and international studio craft.
McKnight is currently planning a future research project focusing on female directors who helmed science films.

clips.text: The translated book was assembled a year after the filmmaker's death by his daughter and features essays tied together by dreams, high-status cultural roundtables, a timeline, and a personal list of favorite movies.

clips.hook: Finding mutual respect at the end
clips.text: Comparing professional rivalries to famous musical duos highlights how two major figures managed to find mutual respect and affection later in life despite a fraught working history.

clips.hook: The vast apprenticeship of a master
clips.text: Working inside a major studio system exposed the director to a wide array of genres and allowed him to learn various production roles while collaborating with numerous mentors.

clips.hook: Planning movies as silent films first
clips.text: The renowned director routinely approached every single film project by visualizing it strictly as a silent movie during the initial planning stages.

clips.hook: The unsolved mystery of a lost silent film
clips.text: Extensive research failed to uncover a single specific silent movie mentioned in the texts where a father accidentally stumbles upon his own son's corpse.

beschreibung:
An interview with Japanese media scholar Anne McNight about her new book Long Take. Long Take is a collection of interviews and other material by or about Akira Kurosawa, one of most famous and influential filmmakers in world history. These are being translated and published into English for the first time.
You can find Dr. McKnight's new translation here:
https://www.upress.umn.edu/9781517903299/long-take/
